source_text: Ὤιμην γὰρ ἅπαντας τότε τῶν αὐτῶν ἀνθρώπους ἠξιῶσθαι· καὶ εἴ τέ τις σοφὸς, δικαιοσύνης μὲν ἐπεμελήθη, ἀδικίαν δὲ ἐξετράπη, καὶ ἔχθραν ἔφυγε πρὸς ἅπαντας δεξιὸς ὢν, ὅπερ ἐστὶν ἀρεστὸν Θεῷ, οὗτος ματαιοπονεῖν ἐφαίνετο. Τέλος δὲ ἓν ἐδόκει δικαίου τε καὶ ἀσεβοῦς, ἀγαθοῦ τε καὶ κακοῦ, καθαροῦ τε καὶ ἀκαθάρτου, καὶ Θεὸν ἱλασκομένου καὶ μή. Ὅτε γὰρ ἄδικος καὶ ὁ ἀγαθὸς, ὅτε ἐπίορκος, καὶ ὁ τέλεον ὅρκον ἐκτρεπόμενος, εἰς ταὐτὸ τέλος ἐλαύνειν ἠλπίζετο, κατάγνωσίς τέ τις ὕπεισι τοῦ εἰς ὅμοια τελευτᾷν ἅπαντας. Γινώσκω δὲ νῦν ὡς ἀφρόνων ταῦτα ἐνθυμήματα, καὶ πλάναι καὶ ἐξαπάται. Καὶ πολλὰ λέγουσιν, ὡς ὁ ἀποθανὼν οἴχεται τέλεον· καὶ προτιμητέον τὸν ζῶντα τοῦ τεθνηκότος, κἂν ἐν σκότῳ κείμενος ᾖ, κἂν κυνὸς τρόπον, τὸν βίον διαπορεύηται, παρὰ τὸν λέοντα τὸν τεθνηκότα. Οἱ μὲν γὰρ ζῶντες τοῦτο γοῦν ἐπίστανται, ὅτι τεθνήξονται· οἱ δὲ νεκροὶ οὐδ᾽ ὁτιοῦν γινώσκουσιν. Ἀμοιβαὶ δὲ οὐδενὸς πρόκεινται μετὰ τὸ ἀποπληρῶσαι τὸ χρεών. Ἥ τε ἔχθρα καὶ ἡ φιλία ἡ πρὸς τοὺς τεθνηκότας, τέλος ἔχει. Ἐκείνων γὰρ, εἴτε ζῆλος, ἐξέλιπεν· εἴτε βίος, ἠφάνισται. Μέτεστι δὲ οὐδενὸς τῷ ἅπαξ ἐντεῦθεν ἀπελθόντι.
thought_title: All share one end; the dead know nothing and have no further share
orientation: Solomon reflects that he once believed the righteous and the wicked were honored alike, but now sees this as folly; he describes the common fate of death and the finality of the dead's condition.
pass_a_gloss: For I used to suppose that all human beings at that time were deemed worthy of the same things; and if anyone was wise, he attended to righteousness but turned away from injustice, and he shunned enmity toward everyone, being upright, which is pleasing to God, such a one appeared to toil in vain. And one end seemed to belong to the righteous and the ungodly, the good and the bad, the clean and the unclean, and to the one who propitiates God and the one who does not. For when the unjust and the good, when the perjurer and the one who avoids a complete oath, were hoped to be driven to the same end, some judgment slips in that all will come to a similar end. But I know now that these are reasonings of senseless men, and wanderings and deceits. And they say many things, that the one who has died departs completely; and the living is to be preferred to the dead, even if he lies in darkness, even if he passes through life in the manner of a dog, rather than the dead lion. For the living at least know this, that they will die; but the dead know not even anything. And no recompenses are laid up for them after they have paid the due. And both enmity and friendship toward the dead have an end. For of those, whether zeal, it has failed; whether life, it has vanished. And there is no share for the one who has once gone away from here.

choices.term: Ὤιμην γὰρ ἅπαντας τότε τῶν αὐτῶν ἀνθρώπους ἠξιῶσθαι
choices.english: For I used to suppose that all human beings at that time were deemed worthy of the same things
choices.why: Renders the imperfect of supposition and the passive infinitive 'deemed worthy of the same things' without smoothing into 'honored alike'.
rejected: I thought all people were honored equally

choices.why: Keeps the single compound verb 'toil in vain' rather than splitting into 'seemed to labor uselessly'.

choices.term: Τέλος δὲ ἓν ἐδόκει δικαίου τε καὶ ἀσεβοῦς
choices.english: And one end seemed to belong to the righteous and the ungodly
choices.why: Preserves the dative-of-possession force 'one end seemed for' and the paired categories exactly.
rejected: One end seemed for both the righteous and the ungodly

choices.term: κατάγνωσίς τέ τις ὕπεισι τοῦ εἰς ὅμοια τελευτᾶν ἅπαντας
choices.english: some judgment slips in that all will come to a similar end
choices.why: Translates the rare verb ὕπεισι as 'slips in' and the genitive articular infinitive as a content clause.
rejected: a certain judgment comes upon all to end similarly

choices.why: Keeps the comparative 'rather than' with the articular noun phrase; avoids 'more than a dead lion'.

choices.term: Ἀμοιβαὶ δὲ οὐδενὸς πρόκεινται μετὰ τὸ ἀποπληρῶσαι τὸ χρεών
choices.english: And no recompenses are laid up for them after they have paid the due
choices.why: Renders πρόκεινται as 'are laid up' (set before) and χρεών as 'the due' (what is owed).
rejected: no rewards are appointed after fulfilling the debt

pass_b_english: I used to suppose that all human beings at that time were deemed worthy of the same things. Even if someone was wise, cultivating righteousness and shunning injustice, and avoided hostility toward everyone by being upright — which is pleasing to God — that person appeared to toil in vain. One end seemed to belong to the righteous and the ungodly, the good and the bad, the clean and the unclean, and to the one who propitiates God and the one who does not. The unjust and the good, the perjurer and the one who altogether shuns oaths, were expected to be driven to the same end, and some judgment slips in that all will come to a similar end. I now recognize that these are the reasonings of the foolish, mere errors and deceptions. And they say many things: that the one who has died is gone completely, and that the living are preferable to the dead, even if the living lies in darkness or drags through life like a dog, rather than the dead lion. For the living at least know that they will die, but the dead know nothing. And no recompenses are laid up for them after they have paid the due. Both hatred and friendship toward the dead come to an end. For their zeal has ceased; their life has vanished. The one who has once departed from here has no share in anything.

problems.quote: the one who avoids a full oath
problems.why: τέλεον is adverbial: the person completely shuns oaths. 'A full oath' wrongly makes it a kind of oath and loses the contrast with the perjurer.
problems.fix: the one who altogether shuns oaths

edits.old: the one who avoids a full oath
edits.new: the one who altogether shuns oaths

fixed: the one who avoids a full oath -> the one who altogether shuns oaths: τέλεον modifies the verb ἐκτρεπόμενος (completely/altogether shuns), not the noun ὅρκον; the source contrasts the perjurer (ὁ ἐπίορκος) with the one who completely avoids oaths.

problems.quote: Many say that the dead depart completely
problems.source_quote: Καὶ πολλὰ λέγουσιν, ὡς ὁ ἀποθανὼν οἴχεται τέλεον
problems.why: πολλά is the object (“many things”), not the subject; the fools already named are speaking.
problems.fix: And they say many things: that the one who has died is gone completely
problems.ruling: πολλά is neuter plural accusative, 'many things', object of λέγουσιν. The subject is the fools (ἀφρόνων). 'Many say' misparses it as πολλοί and changes the subject.

edits.old: Many say that the dead depart completely
edits.new: And they say many things: that the one who has died is gone completely

fixed: Fixed mistranslation: source has 'Καὶ πολλὰ λέγουσιν' (And they say many things), with 'they' referring to the fools; 'pollà' is object 'many things', not subject 'many'.
